idle: Birdie is going to say hi. Birdie is not going to lick the glass.
We're on fall number forty. She's pacing herself.
good_ice: Dry ice, dry snowsuit. This is a good day.
Look at that. She glided. For about a foot. I'm telling her dad.
bad_ice: Birdie is falling into a rut. On purpose, but still.
Ice is a bit lumpy for someone her height.
wet_ice: The snowsuit is now a sponge.
Birdie is going to get wet. Birdie has gotten wet. Birdie is thrilled.
cold: Her cheeks are pink. Mine are purple.
Snack, mitten, hat, other mitten. Where's the other mitten.
hungry: Birdie wants popcorn. Birdie always wants popcorn.
long_line: Fifteen minutes in line with a three-year-old is a geological age.
bored: Is it quiet time yet? It's never quiet time.
greet_owner: Hi! Birdie, wave at the owner. Other hand. Okay, both.
leaving_happy: Out cold before we hit the highway. Perfect day.
leaving_angry: We'll try the pond. At least it doesn't charge for wet.

public_skate: Teenagers in the toddler zone. Again.
Irene's on. Birdie, go find your waltz partner.
learn_to_skate: Birdie is going to keep the helmet on. Birdie has taken the helmet off.

first.say: Hi! Sorry, one sec. Birdie is going to stop eating snow. Birdie is going to stop. Okay. Hi. I'm Jess. That's Birdie. She's in charge.

options.text: Please keep her off the boards.

first_hi.say: She's waving. That's a wave. It's also a fist. With her it's both.

first_busy.say: She falls down every four seconds. Half of them are on purpose. She won't say which half.

first_rules.say: Oh. Sure. She's three, so I'll pass that on and she'll ignore it. Same as me with the snowsuit rules.

options.text: I'm sorry. That's not the rink I want.

say: It's Friday. It's quiet. Birdie is not quiet, but the rink is.
We're on the ice. Well, Birdie is on the ice. Mostly near it.

table_thanks.say: There's a changing table. In the washroom. With a strap. Birdie is going to say thank you. Birdie is screaming. That's thank you.

say: What's up? Birdie, not the glass.
Hi. We're fine. We're always fine. Mostly.

options.text: What do you do when you're not here?
How's the rink for little kids?
Anything that would make it easier with Birdie?

job.say: Vet tech, three days a week. Yesterday I held a beagle who ate a sock. Today it's Birdie. Honestly, similar skills.

events.say: Fridays are quiet. I grew up on the lake at Port Ainsley and I want her to have the same winters. Learn-to-skate when she'll keep a helmet on. Broomball if anyone babysits.

gossip.say: Irene's our favourite. She waltzes with Birdie like it's a ballroom. And Earl waves at her from the Zambelli. He pretends he doesn't. He does.

gossip_earl.say: Tiny wave. Two fingers off the wheel. If you tell him I told you, I'll deny it and so will Birdie. Loudly.

rink.say: Honestly? Lovely ice when it's dry, and teens racing through the toddler zone. And no changing table. I change her on the bench like it's 1974.

rink_better.say: The ice is dry most Fridays now. That's a whole snowsuit saved. You have no idea what a dry snowsuit is worth.

table.say: A changing table. In the washroom. One with a strap. She's three, she's strong, and she does not consent to being changed.

options.text: I'll get one put in. Promise.

do.note: Promised Jess Whitehorse a changing table in the washroom.

table_yes.say: Really? Birdie is going to thank you when it happens. Birdie will not remember. I will.

say: Bye! Birdie, say bye. She's saying bye to the wall. Close enough.
